title: TasksExport
description: tasks-export/1: every document tasks.nvim hands to a machine. One of the kinds below, told apart by `kind`. The engine writes exactly these fields (a field that is not listed fails the contract tests); a reader ignores fields it does not know, because inside one version the contract only grows.

Status.description: The statuses of a task in `ROADMAP/tasks`. `done` is only seen on a task that was left there after it was finished (listed under `unlisted`).

Effort.description: A size (XS to XL) or a duration in days (`3d`, `0.5d`). `effort_days` is always the figure.

Etag.description: The version of a file: `sha256:` and 16 hex digits of the hash of its bytes.

Rev.description: What the vault looked like: `rev:` and 6 hex digits, from every task by id and etag.

Digest.description: The hash of the document's content (without `generated_at` and `engine`): the same vault gives the same digest.

Steps.description: The steps of the optional `## Plan` section; a dropped one is not counted.

Sheets.description: The test-sheet block testing.nvim writes into the task (`testing sheets report --tasks`), from its states line; absent without the block. `state` is the worst sheet (red, stale, never, inbox = green and waiting for a person's judgement, manual, green), `unknown` for a block without a states line. Nothing is run: it is what the last report wrote.

reason.description: Why the state is `unknown`: the block has no states line (an older testing.nvim), no state this engine knows is in it (a newer testing.nvim), or its markers are broken (two blocks, a begin without its end; testing.nvim does not write such a body). Absent otherwise.

Readiness.description: Where a task stands in the plan, from `blocked_by` alone.

stage.description: Absent for a task in a cycle.

rank.description: Position in plan order, 1 is first.

TaskEntry.description: One task. A broken task is still here (`valid: false`, `problems`); a field that is missing is unknown, never 0 (no `effort` means no `effort_days` and no `roi`).

order.description: A tie-breaker inside a stage; a fraction slots a task in between.

roi.description: Value per effort day (never less than a quarter of a day), rounded to two places.

actor_written.description: True when `actor` is what the file says, absent when it was derived.

remind.description: When to look at the task again (a reminder). The date only: whether it is due is for the reader to say, so that a digest does not change with the day.

refs.description: As written, but a path of the machine shows as `<external>/<name>`.

links.description: Web addresses of the task (`http://` or `https://`), apart from `refs`. Only when the task lists any.

open_questions.description: How many questions of the `## Offene Fragen` section of the task are not answered; absent when none is open.

AreaGroup.description: An area group (`<vault>/area-groups.json`, in Neovim also `setup({ area_groups })`): a filter name that stands for several areas. The methods `list`, `order`, `next` and `finished` take a group name for `area` too (`check` takes one area); a write target never is one. Only groups in force are listed (an area of the same name wins).

members.description: The areas of the vault the group stands for, sorted.

Hello.description: tasks.hello: what this engine is and can do. Reads no task.

schemas.description: The versions of the contract this engine speaks.

capabilities.description: What it can answer; show only what is listed.

enums.description: The ranges of the fields, from the engine, so that nobody hard-codes them.

Snapshot.description: tasks.snapshot: one scan, one `rev`: counts, areas, the plan's head, the plan files and every open task with its readiness.

views_rev.description: What the saved views looked like: the `rev` of `tasks.views` (`rev:` and 6 hex digits, from every file of a view by id and etag). A view changed outside changes it (and the digest), not `rev`: a reader that shows the views reads them again when it differs from the one it read.

area_groups.description: The area groups in force with their members; left out when the vault has none.

reminders.description: Finished tasks that carry a reminder (`remind`), the oldest date first, at most 100. An open task's reminder is on its entry; a finished task is not in `tasks`, and a reminder is most often set when a task is finished.

unlisted.description: Task files in `ROADMAP/tasks` that are not open work: a finished task left there, a status nobody knows.

unknown_effort.description: Tasks on the path without an effort (counted as one day each).

conflict_groups.description: Tasks of one stage that name the same file: not parallel work. A list of objects (a tuple would not survive the TypeScript generator).

incomplete.description: Folders that could not be read: the answer may be incomplete.

List.description: tasks.list: one page of tasks in plan order, or in the order the request named (`sort`).

NamedList.description: A named list: a filter and an order under a name. `options` are the option words of the command line (`tasks list --effort=<=S --sort=roi`), a switch is present as `true` and absent when off; a list the engine rejects is not here but in `notes` of the document. `summary` is the one line the engine shows for it (its description, else the words).

NamedLists.description: tasks.lists: the named lists of the engine, read only: the built-in ones, the ones saved with the editor and the ones of the configuration (the later source wins by name), by name. `notes` tell what had to be left out (a rejected definition, a shadowed list, a state file that cannot be read), in the engine's words and without a path of this machine.

Order.description: tasks.order: the ids of the open tasks in the order the request named (`sort`; "default" is the plan's order), all in one document.

Estimate.description: tasks.estimate: the figures of an estimate for some open tasks, also as they would be with other efforts and values (`assume`; nothing is written). The same figures as `estimate` in the snapshot, with the range of the sizes.

range.description: The sum with every size at its low and at its high end: without it the sum looks more exact than it is.

assumed.description: How many of the tasks were taken with assumed values.

PlanFor.description: tasks.planfor: the tasks one task needs before it can start (`needs`) or the tasks that wait for it (`unlocks`), with the hard edges between them, in the order of their distance from the task. The same tasks as `plan --for`.

total.description: All the tasks in the graph; `nodes` holds at most 500 of them.

from.description: The task that has to be finished first.

cycles.description: The cycles whose members are all among `nodes`.

Check.description: tasks.check: the rule check of the vault (`tasks check`), with `stale: refs` also the open tasks that name a file which changed after the task was updated. It reads every task file: a client runs it as a job.

tasks.description: Task files read, open and finished.

total.description: All the findings; `findings` holds at most 1000 of them.

id.description: The task the finding is about, when there is one.

notes.description: What could not be checked (git missing, a budget used up).

Bodies.description: tasks.bodies: the text of many tasks, a page at a time, for a reader that searches it. Its `rev` is that of the snapshot of the same vault.

body.description: The file after the frontmatter, untrusted text.

next_offset.description: Absent on the last page; where to go on when a page ended early (it holds as many bytes as a page may).

TaskDocument.description: tasks.task: one task with its body and steps.

body.description: The file after the frontmatter, untrusted text.

questions.description: The questions of the `## Offene Fragen` / `## Open questions` section, in the order written; empty without the section. A question is answered when exactly one option is ticked; `answer` writes it.

key.description: `q1`; absent for a question written without one (the first `answer` gives it one). `answer` takes the key.

Next.description: tasks.next: what to start, with the reason; or why there is nothing.

cdx.description: Ready tasks an AI session could take, apart from yours.

empty.description: Present when there is no task to start: which kind of nothing it is. `all_done` is only said when nothing is open at all.

Areas.description: tasks.areas: the areas of the vault with their open counts.

area_groups.description: The area groups in force with their members; left out when the vault has none.

FinishedItem.description: A finished task of `Backlog/`: what the engine knows without the plan (a finished task has no readiness). `done` is the day in the file's name; absent for a file without one.

FinishedStats.description: What the finished tasks add up to, over ALL that match the window (not the page). A task that does not carry the field has a row without the key (missing means unknown). The rows of `by_month` and `by_week` are oldest first, the others the biggest first.

effort_days.description: The sum of the efforts that are written down.

without_effort.description: Tasks without an effort (not counted in `effort_days`).

Finished.description: tasks.finished: the finished tasks of the Backlogs, newest first, one page, and what ALL that match add up to. Asked with `since` and `until` (days, both included) it covers the tasks `done` ran for in that window; the area is the one the file is in now.

undated.description: Finished files (of the area asked for) without a `YYYY-MM-DD_` in the name: they are in the figures only when no window is asked for.

LinkEdge.description: One link between the open tasks of two areas, seen from the task it starts at. `to` is the other task (`blocked_by`, `after`) or the plan (`plan`); `ref` is the ref as written (`refs`).

Links.description: tasks.links: where the areas hang together. A link is a `blocked_by` or `after` to an open task of another area, a ref that names another area (`lib.nvim@803de65`, `lib.nvim:anchor`; a path says nothing about the repo), or a plan whose open tasks lie in several areas. `pairs` groups the edges by the two areas (`a` sorts before `b`, the busiest pair first); `tasks` lists, for every open task that touches two or more areas, the areas it touches (its own and those of every link it is part of, in both directions). The edges of the pairs are cut at 2000 (`truncated`); `edge_count`, the counts and `tasks` cover all of them.

Groupings.description: tasks.groupings: the fields the open tasks can be grouped by, with the values each can have and how a reader writes it. `status`, `prio`, `actor`, `kind`, `effort` and `value` are the model's; `tags`, `plan` and `phase` are the ones the open tasks name (at most 200, `truncated` says the rest); `area` is the areas of the vault; `state` and `cross` are derived (`cross`: `several` for a task `tasks.links` names among the tasks that touch two or more areas, else `one`). `mode` says which operation writes the field: `set` (a field of the file), `tags` (the list of tags: leaving one and taking another is one `set` of the whole list) or `move_area`; a field without `mode` is read only. The same `rev` as the snapshot of the same vault.

View.description: One saved view: a selection (which tasks), a grouping (by which field, a matrix by a second one) and how it is drawn. It holds no task and no rule. `etag` is the version of its file: a change is made on it (`view_save`, `view_delete`).

group_by2.description: The field of the rows of a matrix (never the field of the columns).

collapsed.description: The groups that are folded (the values as `tasks.groupings` names them).

ViewSelect.description: Which tasks a view shows: every list narrows (an empty list does not), `query` is a word the title must hold.

Views.description: tasks.views: the saved views of the vault (`<area>/ROADMAP/views/<slug>.md`), sorted by id. A file that cannot be read as a view is no view but a line of `problems`. The `rev` is that of the views, not of the tasks.

Error.description: tasks.error: what went wrong, in a code that is stable. `message` carries no path of the machine.

ErrorCode.description: Why something failed, in a word that is stable. A reader treats a word it does not know as `internal`.

OperationError.description: Why an operation did not happen. `details` names ids, keys and values (`expected` and `actual` of a conflict, the `problems` of a refused relation), never a path.

Inverse.description: The operation that undoes a change: send it as a new operation (its `if_match` is the version the change left). A key the change added is `null` in the patch of a `set`.

done.description: `tick_step`: whether the step is to be ticked (true) or open (false).

clear.description: `answer`: true when no option was ticked, the question was open.

body.description: `set_body`: the text below the frontmatter that the task had.

to_area.description: `move_area`: the area the task came from (`id` is the id it has now).

view.description: `view_save`: the view as it was (a `view_save` with it puts it back).

MovePlan.description: What moving a task to another area would do and break (stage 1 of `move_area`: a report, nothing is written).

references.description: Places that name the old id and would dangle.

ResultEntry.description: What happened to one operation of a request, in the order they were sent. A failed operation does not stop the others.

outcome.description: `would_*` is what a dry run says; `blocked` is a move that cannot be made.

restore.description: What a reorder wrote: these `set` operations give every file it wrote its old `order` back (send them all instead of `inverse`, which only restores the place: a task that had no `order` would keep one, and the neighbours the move numbered stay numbered).

changed_ids.description: Ids whose files this operation wrote (a dry run: none).

index.description: What happened to the generated index of the area, once for the whole request.

slug.description: `plan_new`: the file name (without `.md`) the plan got or would get.

renamed.description: `plan_new`: the slug asked for was taken, so another one was chosen.

asset.description: `attach`: the path of the new asset below the task folder, e.g. `assets/shot.png`.

link.description: `attach`: the Markdown that links the asset (an image gets `![name](path)`), to put into the task.

new_id.description: `move_area`: the id the task has after the move.

rewritten.description: `move_area`: the places that named the old id and now name the new one.

Result.description: tasks.result: the answer to a request of `tasks-ops/1`, one entry per operation. `ok` is true only when every operation was.

DonePreview.description: tasks.donepreview: what finishing a task would do, with nothing written, and the `confirm` token that `done` needs for exactly this version of the file.

already.description: The task is finished already: nothing to confirm.

closes_plan.description: The plan this finish closes: the task is its last open member.

freed.description: Open tasks that wait on nothing but this one.
